newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- APRIL 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- APRIL 17.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Dramatic developments in Greek-Turkish relations were announced by Dutch Foreign Minister and European Union Council President Hans Van Mierlo in Malta yesterday. Van Mierlo said there was a "lifting of the impasse" between Athens and Ankara over their Aegean dispute, implying that there had been an in-principle agreement thrashed out between Deputy Foreign Minister George Papandreou and his Turkish counterpart Onur Oymen at Malta's Euro-Mediterranean conference yesterday.

--Hospitals, universities, and other institutions and organisations subsidised by the state are lacking basic accounting procedures and practices, according to reports. The economic chaos is chronic, reports say.

--Judicial officials have begun a preliminary investigation into claims and counter-claims of blackmail and pressure between Stavros Psyharis, the editor of Sunday paper 'To Vima', and Dimitris Rizos, of daily 'Adesmeftos Typos'. A meeting between the two and a businessman involved in the supply of natural gas is reported to have been about forcing the businessman to involve another leading businessman in certain ventures.

--Yesterday's conference in Malta provided the backdrop to Greece's step away from the impasse with Turkey over disputes in bilateral relations. The establishment of a committee of "wise men" is expected to assist in the resolution of disputes.

--Today will see more fat added to the Papandreou fire as George Liani, cousin to Andreas Papandreou's widow Dimitra, launches his book "Andreas Papandreou - The Last Leader", an insider's appraisal of the last years of ruling PASOK's late founder and president. The book comes days after Papandreou's children launched a lawsuit to reclaim a house sold by Papandreou to build his new wife a luxurious villa.
--Meanwhile, the counter-suit filed by the present occupant of the house against Dimitra Liani will be heard in an Athens court next Tuesday.

--Work at the tax department has stacked up and the finance ministry is ordering employees to quicken the pace. More than three million declarations have yet to be submitted to the appropriate department for checking.

--Nobody is entirely without blame for the Imia incident last year that almost brought Greece and Turkey to war, former Greek chief of staff Christos Lymberis says. Lymberis was chief of the armed forces at the time and was later relieved of his position.
--A new book claims that former dictator George Papadopoulos began planning a coup as early as 1963, with the full knowledge of the US.
--Electricity, postage, tolls, airfares and public transport will all be more expensive on July 1 this year.
--New Democracy president Costas Karamanlis shows his colours as he attends an AEK-Panathinaikos soccer match.

--Greek troops left for Albania yesterday with hopes for their safe tour of duty sealed with a kiss from relatives and friends who saw them off in Thessaloniki yesterday. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
